conceptPrimer.heading: Bohr Model for One-Electron Species
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: For hydrogenic ions ($\text{H}, \text{He}^+, \text{Li}^{2+}$) of nuclear charge $Z$, Bohr's quantization $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$ gives orbit radius $r_n = 0.529\,\frac{n^2}{Z}\ \text{\AA}$, speed $v_n \propto \frac{Z}{n}$ and total energy $E_n = -13.6\,\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\ \text{eV}$, with kinetic energy $K = -E$ and potential energy $U = 2E$. Every quantity scales with $Z$ and $n$ — no new physics per ion. Micro-check: $\text{He}^+$ ground state: $E_1 = -13.6 \times 2^2 = -54.4\ \text{eV}$, and $K = +54.4\ \text{eV}$, $U = -108.8\ \text{eV}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Rydberg Formula and Spectral Series
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: A transition $n_2 \to n_1$ emits a photon of wavenumber $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$ with $R_H = 1.097 \times 10^7\ \text{m}^{-1}$. Series are named by the FIXED lower level: Lyman ($n_1 = 1$, UV), Balmer ($n_1 = 2$, visible), Paschen ($n_1 = 3$, IR). Electrons falling from a level $n_2$ can land through every intermediate level, producing $\frac{\Delta n(\Delta n + 1)}{2}$ distinct lines. Micro-check: from $n = 4$ to $n = 2$: $\Delta n = 2$ gives $\frac{2 \times 3}{2} = 3$ lines ($4 \to 3$, $4 \to 2$, $3 \to 2$).

conceptPrimer.heading: Quantum Numbers and Node Counting
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Four numbers label every electron: principal $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$; azimuthal $l = 0 \dots n-1$ ($s, p, d, f$); magnetic $m_l = -l \dots +l$ giving $2l+1$ orbitals per subshell, $n^2$ orbitals and $2n^2$ maximum electrons per shell; spin $m_s = \pm\frac{1}{2}$. Nodes are counted from the same pair: angular (planar/conical) nodes $= l$, radial (spherical) nodes $= n - l - 1$, total $= n - 1$. Micro-check: a $4d$ orbital ($n = 4, l = 2$) has $2$ angular and $4 - 2 - 1 = 1$ radial nodes, $3$ total.

conceptPrimer.heading: Filling Rules: Aufbau, Pauli, Hund and the Cr/Cu Exceptions
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Subshells fill in increasing $n + l$; on a tie the lower $n$ wins, so $4s$ ($4+0$) fills before $3d$ ($3+2=5$). Pauli exclusion forbids two electrons sharing all four quantum numbers (hence $2$ per orbital), and Hund's rule spreads electrons parallel-spin across degenerate orbitals first. Half-filled and fully-filled subshells gain exchange stability, so $\text{Cr}$ ($Z = 24$) is $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^5 4s^1$ and $\text{Cu}$ ($Z = 29$) is $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^{10} 4s^1$. Micro-check: order around $n = 4$: $3p \to 4s \to 3d \to 4p$ — $4s$ wins the tie against $3d$ on $n$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Spin-Only Magnetic Moment and Ion Configurations
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Paramagnetism comes from unpaired electrons only: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{BM}$. For transition-metal IONS, remove electrons from $4s$ FIRST (it filled first but leaves first), then recount the $d$-shell. $\text{Fe}$: $[\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^2 \to \text{Fe}^{2+}$: $[\text{Ar}]3d^6$ with $4$ unpaired — never $3d^4 4s^2$. Micro-check: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$, so $n = 5$: $\mu = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35} \approx 4.9 \times 1.21 \approx 5.92\ \text{BM}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: de Broglie Waves and the Uncertainty Principle
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Matter waves: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{mv}$ — measurable only for particles of subatomic mass. An electron accelerated through $V$ volts has $K = eV$, giving the handy $\lambda(\text{\AA}) = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}$. Heisenberg's principle caps simultaneous precision: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$ (note the $4\pi$, not $2\pi$). Micro-check: electron through $V = 100\ \text{V}$: $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{100}} = 1.227\ \text{\AA}$ — atomic-scale, hence electron diffraction works.

keyDefinitions.definition: Orbit: fixed classical path (Bohr). Orbital: probability-density region $|\psi|^2$ (quantum model).
Ground: lowest energy ($n = 1$ for H). Excited: any $n > $ ground; reached by absorbing a photon.
Line families named by the fixed lower level $n_1$: Lyman ($1$, UV), Balmer ($2$, visible), Paschen ($3$, IR), Brackett ($4$), Pfund ($5$).
Sets shell, size and (with $Z$) energy: allowed $1, 2, 3, \dots$
$l$ sets subshell shape ($0$–$n{-}1$) and node count; $m_l$ ($-l \dots +l$) sets orbital orientation.
$\pm\frac{1}{2}$ — two electrons per orbital, opposite spins (Pauli).
Radial: sphere of zero $|\psi|^2$ counted by $n - l - 1$. Angular: plane/cone counted by $l$.
No two electrons in an atom share all four quantum numbers.
Degenerate orbitals fill singly, parallel-spin, before pairing.
Different species with the same electron count ($\text{O}^{2-}, \text{F}^-, \text{Ne}, \text{Na}^+$: $10\ e^-$).

mcqSelfTest.explanation: $E_1 = -13.6\,Z^2 = -13.6 \times 9 = -122.4\ \text{eV}$. One-electron species only — this is exactly why Bohr works for $\text{Li}^{2+}$ but not neutral Li.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Electrons dropping from $n = 4$ directly to the Balmer level $n_1 = 2$ can produce how many distinct lines?
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\Delta n = 4 - 2 = 2$: $N = \frac{\Delta n(\Delta n + 1)}{2} = \frac{2 \times 3}{2} = 3$ — the jumps $4 \to 3$, $4 \to 2$ and $3 \to 2$.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: How many radial nodes does a $3p$ orbital have?
The ratio $r(\text{He}^+, n = 2) : r(\text{H}, n = 1)$ of Bohr radii is:

mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is $3d^{10}$ — fully filled, zero unpaired. $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($d^3$), $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($d^5$) all retain unpaired electrons.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: In Aufbau $(n+l)$ filling, the subshell filled immediately AFTER $4s$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $4s$ ($4+0 = 4$) then $3d$ ($3+2 = 5$): within equal $n+l$... here $3d$ and $4p$ both total $5$, but lower $n$ wins, so $3d$ first.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: An electron accelerated through $V = 100\ \text{V}$ has de Broglie wavelength:
If the permitted uncertainty $\Delta x$ in position is halved, the minimum uncertainty $\Delta p$ in momentum:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$: the product floor is fixed, so halving one factor forces the other to double.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The total number of orbitals in the shell $n = 3$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $n^2 = 9$ orbitals ($1 \times 3s + 3 \times 3p + 5 \times 3d$); $18$ would be the maximum ELECTRON count $2n^2$.

memoryHooks: Energy carries $Z^2$, radius only $Z$ — and both sit under $n^2$ (radius) or $n^2$ (energy).
$K = -E$, $U = 2E$: kinetic is what the energy owes.
Angular nodes $= l$, radial $= n - l - 1$, total $= n - 1$.
$4s$ fills before $3d$ — but $4s$ LEAVES first when an ion forms.
Cr wants five half-filled $d$'s; Cu wants a full $d^{10}$.
$\sqrt{n(n+2)}$: count UNPAIRED electrons, never the total.
Lyman ends at $n = 1$ (UV); Balmer ends at $n = 2$ (visible); Paschen at $3$ (IR).
Bohr math is a one-electron club: H, $\text{He}^+$, $\text{Li}^{2+}$ only.
Lines from one jump level: $\frac{\Delta n(\Delta n+1)}{2}$.
commonMistakes: Stripping $3d$ before $4s$ when forming transition-metal ions (Fe²⁺ is $3d^6$, not $3d^4 4s^2$).
Applying Bohr energies to neutral He or any multi-electron species.
Swapping angular ($l$) and radial ($n - l - 1$) node counts.
Using $h/2\pi$ instead of $h/4\pi$ in the uncertainty product.
Quoting $2l + 1$ as the ELECTRON capacity of a subshell (that's orbitals; electrons are $2(2l+1)$).
Ordering subshells by $n$ alone instead of $n + l$.
Dropping the minus sign or the $Z^2$ when scaling $E_n$.
Reporting $\mu$ in any unit other than Bohr magneton (BM).
examChecklist: Confirm the species is one-electron BEFORE any Bohr formula.
Scale with $Z^2/n^2$ for energy, $n^2/Z$ for radius, $Z/n$ for speed.
Name the series from the FIXED lower level $n_1$.
Fill by $n + l$; break ties toward lower $n$.
For ions: remove $4s$ electrons first, then recount unpaired.
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM with the corrected unpaired count.
$\Delta x \Delta p \ge h/4\pi$; de Broglie $\lambda = 12.27/\sqrt{V}$ Å for electrons.
Convert eV ↔ J with $1.602 \times 10^{-19}$ when the answer wants SI.
